name: Asan PCI robot
full_name: Asan Medical Center modular bi-motional roller-cartridge PCI robot
group: Asan Medical Center, University of Ulsan College of Medicine (Jaesoon Choi; Dept. of Cardiology, Young-Hak Kim; Dept. of Convergence Medicine, Youngjin Moon) (choi2021_vascular p. 1)
versions: choi2021_vascular (Biosensors 2021); 2017-18: Asan (J. Choi) EP platform driving a commercial ablation (steerable) catheter with rolling belts, leader with a 3-RRR planar manipulator (Moon 2018), ex vivo phantom (Hu 2017) (Alekseeva 2025 Table 3 row 7, Fig. 8f; Belikov 2024 Fig. 5 HU1) (alekseeva2025_design; belikov2024_evolution); 2020-21: Asan (J. Choi, Y.-H. Kim) cardiac-ablation catheter robot: dual-gripper front module inserts and rotates the catheter without slip, handle module turns the bending knob, Jacobian updated from two position sensors on the catheter (Lee 2021 J. Mech. Robot. 13, doi:10.1115/1.4048224) (Belikov 2024 Fig. 5 LE) (lee2021_design; belikov2024_evolution); 2021: deep RL (Rainbow) guidewire navigation trained and tested on the physical 2-D and 3-D coronary phantoms with an Asan robotic module whose opposed roller pair advances the wire and whose vertical roller shift rotates it, step 0.4 mm or 33 deg (Kweon 2021 IEEE Access; Konda 2025 control row 33); real-world training, not sim-to-real (kweon2021_deep; konda2025_robotically)
devices_driven: three modules drive a guiding catheter, a guidewire and a balloon catheter (Sec. 2.1.2, p. 3), 3 devices at once; the clamping also fits guide extensions and IVUS catheters (p. 2); bench devices 5 F catheter, 0.014-in guidewire, 3.5 x 15 mm balloon (p. 10); in vivo only the guidewire was robot-driven (p. 13-16)
n_dof_detail: 8 by our sum (paper gives no total): guiding-catheter and guidewire modules 3-DOF each (clamp, translate, rotate), balloon module 2-DOF (choi2021_vascular Sec. 2.1.2, p. 3)
translation_detail: friction-roller (tightly pressed roller pairs, 20 mm rollers driven through bevel gears) (choi2021_vascular Sec. 2.1.1, p. 2-3)
rotation_detail: Roller pair rubs the device: a motor, bevel gear and ball screw raise the cartridge frame; limited range of about 900-1800 degrees from a 25 mm vertical displacement (Sec. 2.3.2, p. 7); clamping by motor, timing belt and bidirectional ball screw (p. 4)
device_range: accommodates instruments of various sizes via the active clamping mechanism; rotation range about 900-1800 degrees per cartridge stroke (p. 7); translation stroke and speeds N.R.
force_sensing: none: no force sensor; the haptic cue is a virtual wall near the cartridge rotation limit, computed from cartridge position (choi2021_vascular Discussion, p. 17)
haptics_leader: master: 3-RRR planar parallel mechanism + linear actuator ('clutch-like trigger') + spherical wrist mechanism, called a 6-DOF mechanism (Sec. 2.1.3, p. 4-5; p. 17), Maxon DC motors; force feedback used only as a virtual wall
imaging_compat: real-time fluoroscopy on the console monitors; physician behind radiation-shielded glass (choi2021_vascular p. 5, Fig. 17b)
sterility: roller cartridge designed as a disposable part (p. 4); sterile drapes and detachable sterilised rollers form the sterile interface, no closed housing (p. 15, 17)
validation_detail: bench: 20 cartridge-gap trials, 10 repetitions per translation length and per 360-degree rotation; phantom: EVE silicone model, trial count N.R.; animal: one 60 kg pig, robot-driven guidewire into the RCA; clinical: 2 patients (coronary angiography), robot-driven guidewire to the LAD and the RCA, both technically successful; MFDS approval 20190064902 (choi2021_vascular p. 9-16)
key_numbers: translation mean error: guiding catheter -0.93 to 0.75 mm, guidewire 0.11-0.86 mm, balloon 0.07-0.57 mm (Table 1); rotation error at 360 degrees: guiding catheter 3.29 +- 5.48, guidewire 1.93 +- 2.50 degrees (Table 2) (choi2021_vascular)
